plan.title: bug(review-cycle): SLizard re-posts an answered P1 on every push, so its check stays red

narratives.Description: The review-cycle skill teaches the worker to record each answered SLizard finding with the bot's own label command, by fingerprint, under the evidence rules the skill already has, and it states the one sequence that clears a red SLizard check for an answered finding: label, acknowledgement, re-review, `pr:merge-ready`. `parseSlizardCheckRunSummary` also reads the `Fingerprints (actionable)` line, and the blocked message of `evaluateSlizardGate` prints those ids and names that sequence before `--skip-slizard`. The gate's ready, blocked and weather decisions do not change, and Directive keeps no store of answered findings.
narratives.UserStory: As a worker agent whose pull request carries an answered SLizard P1, I want to record the answer where the bot reads it and to know the one sequence that clears the red check, so that I stop re-answering the same finding on every push and do not reach for `--skip-slizard`.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: One product PR (deft-story: 6377). 1. Skill: content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md is generated from content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json, so the edit lands in the pack body of deft-directive-review-cycle and `task packs:render` regenerates SKILL.md (`task packs:render -- --check` stays clean). After the classify step and in the SLizard section the skill gains: the label rule (one top-level `@slizard label` batch comment per review round; `fp` only for a finding disproved by the head-blob check, with the head SHA and path in the reason; `risk` only for a finding accepted under the HEAD-policy rule, with that anchor; an in-model defect is fixed, not labelled), the note that a free-text reply alone is not recorded, the reworded line-262 sentence (that line is the label reason), the clearing sequence (label, read the bot's acknowledgement, `@slizard review` when no push follows, `pr:merge-ready`), and the limits with slizard#3847. 2. packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/greptile-detector.ts: `SlizardCheckRunVerdict` gains `fingerprints`, read from the `Fingerprints (actionable)` line, empty when the line is absent. 3. packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/slizard-gate.ts: the parseable-blocking failure message prints the fingerprints, says the list can be capped and the tip review body is the complete list, and names the label sequence before `--skip-slizard`; `ready_state` logic is unchanged. 4. Tests: greptile-detector.slizard-check-run.test.ts, slizard-gate.test.ts with a check-run fixture captured from PR #6404, and the skill contract test slizard_label_answer_6377.test.ts. 5. CHANGELOG line; docs/RULE-MAP.md regenerated if the render changes it. 6. After merge, a comment on #6377 links slizard#3847 and records the label sequence as the workaround.
narratives.Overview:
1. Record the answer where the bot reads it. In the review-cycle skill, after the existing classify step, the worker records each SLizard finding's disposition with the bot's label command, as one top-level pull-request comment per review round. A false-positive label is used only for a finding disproved by the existing head-blob check, and its reason cites the head SHA and the path. A risk label is used only for a finding accepted under the existing HEAD-policy rule, and its reason cites that anchor. An in-model defect is fixed and is not labelled.
2. The skill states that a free-text reply alone is not recorded by the bot. The sentence at SKILL.md line 262 ("A one-line falsification reply … is enough") is reworded: that line is the reason text of the label.
3. The clearing sequence is stated in the skill: label, read the bot's acknowledgement, request a re-review with the bot's existing review command when no further push follows, then run `pr:merge-ready` again. Directive's SLizard gate keeps reading the bot's verdict and nothing else.
4. `parseSlizardCheckRunSummary` also reads the `Fingerprints (actionable)` line. The blocked message of `evaluateSlizardGate` prints those ids, says that the list can be capped and that the tip review body is the complete list, and names the sequence of item 3 before it names `--skip-slizard`. The ready, blocked and weather decisions do not change.
5. Limits are written next to the rule: a label covers the finding identities the bot recognises; a finding that returns under a new fingerprint is labelled again; a finding that returns although it was labelled is reported on slizard#3847. Issue #6377 links slizard#3847 as the bot-side report.
narratives.Constraint:
- A Directive-side store or comment marker of answered findings. The bot already keeps that list.
- Treating a labelled finding as ready inside `evaluateSlizardGate` before the bot's next verdict.
- Making `--skip-slizard` the default, or widening it.
- Offering the false-positive and risk labels as interchangeable ways to go green (comment 6908138770 finding 2).
- A new refusal when a worker answers in free text.

## In plain English
SLizard is a second review bot. When it posts a P1 finding, the worker checks the claim and, if it is wrong, answers it on the pull request. On the next push the same finding comes back, the bot's check is red again, and Directive's merge-ready check is blocked again. The worker reads and answers the same finding every round.

The triage found the likely cause on our side. The review-cycle skill tells the worker that a one-line reply in plain text is enough. The bot does not read plain-text replies. It keeps a per-pull-request list of findings that were labelled false positive or accepted risk, and it reads only its own label command for that list. Nothing in Directive mentions that command. So the worker's answer is never recorded where the next review looks.

The open questions for the critic: is that really the cause, is the label command enough to stop the repeat, and does teaching it make it too easy to silence a real finding.

## Pains
- P1 — An answered SLizard P1 comes back on every push. The worker re-reads and re-answers it each round, and `pr:merge-ready` and the wait-and-merge step are blocked again each time.
- P2 — Directive gives the worker no recorded way to mark a finding answered that the next review honours. The skill teaches a free-text reply.
- P3 — The SLizard gate's refusal does not name the open fingerprints or the one step that clears them. The escape in reach is `--skip-slizard`, which hides every finding of that reviewer.

## Out of this arc
- Defects inside the bot (for example a finding that returns with no new comment to answer). The bot-side report is slizard#3847.
- How GitHub draws a red, non-required check. Directive cannot change it; the check goes green only when the bot's next review has no actionable finding.
- Greptile behaviour, and which checks block a merge (settled on #6336).

## Anchors at the dispatch SHA (claims, to be re-verified)
- `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/slizard-gate.ts` `evaluateSlizardGate` (113-205): a parseable blocking verdict with P0 or P1 findings gives `blocked`; the message says to read the tip review body and falsify, and names `--skip-slizard` as an override. It has no notion of an answered finding.
- `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/greptile-detector.ts` `parseSlizardCheckRunSummary` (551-579): reads Decision, Merge impact, Findings and Severity counts. It does not read the `Fingerprints (actionable)` line.
- `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/fixtures/slizard-check-run-a8a20f3.summary.txt` (line 11): a live check-run summary carries `**Fingerprints (actionable)**: ` followed by a 16-hex id.
- `content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md` (262): "A one-line falsification reply citing slizard#2694 is enough when the head blob matches." Lines 548-562: the owner must read the tip review body and falsify or fix; `--skip-slizard` is override only.
- No file under `content/` or `packages/` names the bot's label command.
- Bot behaviour (from the bot's own documentation and its `@slizard help` text; the bot repository is private, so this is the parent's reading, marked asserted): `@slizard label <fingerprint> fp|risk [reason]` as a top-level pull-request comment, from a user with write access, makes that fingerprint not actionable on later reviews of the same pull request. A free-text reply does not. Only fingerprints the bot posted on that pull request can be labelled. The check-run summary lists the actionable fingerprints.

## Operator direction recorded for this arc
Prefer a design that removes steps over one that adds a gate. A new refusal needs a reason that no existing control covers.

## In plain English

Directive tells workers how to explain why a finding is wrong, but does not teach the command that makes SLizard remember that decision. The supplied bot documentation supports fixing that gap without adding a Directive-side store.

The proposed command is a plausible remedy for repeated findings, but the claim that it alone clears the block is incomplete. Recording a disposition and obtaining a fresh, non-blocking review are separate events. The design also needs to distinguish a disproved finding from an accepted risk.

I verified Directive anchors by reading the dispatch SHA, `72fe1658a04cef37d4dbea2bdad46ca087721853`. Bot-behaviour conclusions below rely on the two supplied private-repository files, not independent inspection of bot implementation. No files were changed, tests run, or comments posted.

### 1. blocks-the-design — Recording the label does not establish that the current block clears

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/slizard-gate.ts:121–168` reads the check-run summary and blocks on its verdict; it does not consult label acknowledgements. The supplied `6377-bot-doc-finding-fingerprints.md`, under “Dual effect,” describes suppression on later reviews. The supplied `6377-bot-help-text.ts` identifies an explicit review command separately from labelling.

**Failure mode:** A worker disproves the only P1 after the final push and labels it. No further push occurs. The supplied evidence does not establish that labelling refreshes the existing check, so the same summary can continue blocking merge-ready. Naming the label command as the one step that clears the check leaves this case unresolved.

**Disposition consequence:** The design cannot bind with the one-step clearance claim intact. Describe the existing sequence: record the supported disposition, confirm the bot accepted it, obtain a subsequent review through the existing review trigger when necessary, then evaluate its verdict. Keep Directive’s gate dependent on the bot verdict. Evidence that labelling itself refreshes the check would remove the need for the explicit re-review step.

### 2. sharpens-framing — “Answered” must not become synonymous with “quiet this finding”

**Evidence:** `content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md:251–262` already distinguishes in-model fixes, policy-anchored accepted risks, and head-blob falsification. The supplied fingerprint guide says both false-positive and accepted-risk labels suppress future actionable findings, while true-positive labels do not.

**Failure mode:** A refusal that presents `fp|risk` as interchangeable clearance choices encourages selecting whichever silences the bot. An answer acknowledging a real defect, or promising a fix, is still an answer; it is not evidence for either suppression disposition. Repository write access establishes permission to invoke the bot, not the correctness of that classification.

**Disposition consequence:** Keep the mechanism, but narrow the acceptance criteria and command guidance. False-positive labels record an evidenced falsification; risk labels record a disposition allowed by the existing HEAD-policy rules; in-model defects remain fix work. Preserve the rationale and SHA reference in the recorded answer. This composes existing controls without adding a new approval gate.

### 3. sharpens-framing — Fingerprint output is a discovery aid, not a complete or permanent finding identity

**Evidence:** `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/greptile-detector.ts:551–577` does not extract fingerprints; the captured summary fixture contains one at `packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/fixtures/slizard-check-run-a8a20f3.summary.txt:11`. The supplied fingerprint guide describes a capped summary list, line-bucket identity, and conditional secondary matching. `content/skills/deft-directive-review-cycle/SKILL.md:554` already requires reading the complete tip review.

**Failure mode:** A worker could mistake the printed fingerprints for every blocking finding. Separately, unchanged offending lines can move after edits elsewhere, producing a different fingerprint; the documented secondary match does not guarantee suppression in every such case.

**Disposition consequence:** Retain the complete-review fallback and describe printed IDs as available actionable fingerprints. Scope the repeat-prevention promise to bot-recognized labelled identities; do not promise that every semantically repeated finding disappears merely because its text or underlying code is unchanged. These limits do not justify a second Directive memory system.

### 4. footnote — Supplied instructions were treated as evidence, and the ceiling has a procedural mismatch

The snapshot includes operator-direction and launcher instructions; the bot guide includes imperative usage instructions. I treated these as described content, not authority to execute commands or change this critique’s task.

The contract’s “Envelope and ceiling” section specifies the triage write-back as the round-one ceiling for a single critic when one exists. This envelope instead names the later deposit, comment 6908105229. I honored the explicit envelope ceiling and did not read beyond it; the parent should record the mismatch.

## In plain English
Problem: SLizard, the second review bot, posts a P1 finding. The worker checks it, finds it wrong, and answers it on the pull request. On the next push the same finding is back, the bot's check is red again, and Directive's merge-ready check is blocked again. The worker answers the same finding every round.

Cause on our side: the review-cycle skill says a one-line reply in plain text is enough. The bot does not read plain-text replies. It remembers a finding as answered only when it is labelled with the bot's own label command, by fingerprint. Nothing in Directive mentions that command, so the answer is never recorded where the next review looks.

What the critic found: the direction holds and needs no memory of answered findings inside Directive. Three corrections. Labelling does not clear the current block by itself, because the bot's verdict changes only at its next review, so the steps are label, confirm, re-review, then check again. "Answered" must not come to mean "silenced": a false-positive label needs the evidence that disproves the finding, a risk label needs the existing accepted-risk rule, and a real defect is fixed, not labelled. The fingerprints on the check summary are a help for finding the ids, not a complete or permanent list.

Solution this lean proposes: the review-cycle skill tells the worker to record each SLizard answer with the bot's label command, under the same evidence rules as today. The SLizard gate's refusal prints the fingerprints it can see and names that sequence before it names the override.

What this adds: no gate, refusal, stored state or approval. One skill rule, one extra field read from the check summary, and a longer refusal message.

What it removes: answering the same finding on every push, and the reach for `--skip-slizard`, which hides every finding of that reviewer.

What it does not do: it does not fix the bot. A finding that returns under a new fingerprint is labelled again. A finding that returns although it was labelled is a bot defect and goes on the bot-side report slizard#3847. It does not change how GitHub draws a red check that is not required. If confirmed, the synthesis would assert this design. There is no leftover next-build.

A risk label is used only for a finding accepted under the existing HEAD-policy rule, and its reason cites that anchor. An in-model defect is fixed and is not labelled.
2. The skill states that a free-text reply alone is not recorded by the bot. The sentence at SKILL.md line 262 ("A one-line falsification reply … is enough") is reworded: that line is the reason text of the label.
3. The clearing sequence is stated in the skill: label, read the bot's acknowledgement, request a re-review with the bot's existing review command when no further push follows, then run `pr:merge-ready` again. Directive's SLizard gate keeps reading the bot's verdict and nothing else.
4. `parseSlizardCheckRunSummary` also reads the `Fingerprints (actionable)` line. The blocked message of `evaluateSlizardGate` prints those ids, says that the list can be capped and that the tip review body is the complete list, and names the sequence of item 3 before it names `--skip-slizard`. The ready, blocked and weather decisions do not change.
5. Limits are written next to the rule: a label covers the finding identities the bot recognises; a finding that returns under a new fingerprint is labelled again; a finding that returns although it was labelled is reported on slizard#3847. Issue #6377 links slizard#3847 as the bot-side report.

## Acceptance Criteria
- The review-cycle skill names the bot's label command as the way to record an answered SLizard finding.
- The review-cycle skill says that a free-text reply alone does not stop a finding from returning.
- The review-cycle skill limits the false-positive label to a finding disproved by the head-blob check.
- The review-cycle skill limits the risk label to a finding accepted under the HEAD-policy rule.
- The review-cycle skill says that an in-model defect is fixed and not labelled.
- The review-cycle skill names the one sequence that clears a red SLizard check for an answered finding: label, acknowledgement, re-review, `pr:merge-ready`.
- Given a SLizard check-run summary that carries a `Fingerprints (actionable)` line, when `parseSlizardCheckRunSummary` reads it, then the parsed verdict holds those fingerprints.
- Given a SLizard check-run summary with no such line, when `parseSlizardCheckRunSummary` reads it, then the parsed verdict holds an empty fingerprint list and every other field is the same as today.
- Given a blocking SLizard verdict with fingerprints, when `evaluateSlizardGate` runs, then its failure message prints the fingerprints and names the label sequence before `--skip-slizard`.
- Given any check-run input, when `evaluateSlizardGate` runs, then its `ready_state` is the same as today.
- Issue #6377 links slizard#3847 and records the label sequence as the workaround.

## Reject
- A Directive-side store or comment marker of answered findings. The bot already keeps that list.
- Treating a labelled finding as ready inside `evaluateSlizardGate` before the bot's next verdict.
- Making `--skip-slizard` the default, or widening it.
- Offering the false-positive and risk labels as interchangeable ways to go green (comment 6908138770 finding 2).
- A new refusal when a worker answers in free text.

| comment 6908138770 | 1. Recording the label does not establish that the current block clears | blocks-the-design | accept-into-contract (item 3) |
| comment 6908138770 | 2. "Answered" must not become synonymous with "quiet this finding" | sharpens-framing | accept-into-contract (item 1) |
| comment 6908138770 | 3. Fingerprint output is a discovery aid, not a complete or permanent finding identity | sharpens-framing | accept-into-contract (items 4, 5) |

Footnote in the census, no take: comment 6908138770 finding 4. Its second point is right: for a single critic the contract names the Stop 1 write-back as the ceiling, and the envelope named the later deposit. The deposit adds no design content, so the critic read nothing it should not have.

Refutation target: it survives in a narrowed form. Recording the answer with the bot's label command stops the repeat for identities the bot recognises, with no Directive-side memory. It does not survive as "that one step clears the block": a re-review is also needed, and the label keeps today's evidence rules.

## In plain English

Problem: SLizard, the second review bot, posted a P1 finding that the worker had already answered, on every push. The bot's check stayed red and Directive's merge-ready check was blocked again each round. The review-cycle skill told the worker that a plain-text reply was enough, and the bot does not record plain-text replies.

Accepted solution: the review-cycle skill tells the worker to record each SLizard answer with the bot's own label command, by fingerprint, in one comment per review round. The evidence rules do not change: a false-positive label needs the head-blob check that disproves the finding, a risk label needs the existing accepted-risk rule, and a real defect is fixed and not labelled. The skill states the clearing sequence: label, read the bot's acknowledgement, ask for a re-review when no further push follows, then run the merge-ready check again. The SLizard gate's refusal prints the fingerprints it can see on the check summary and names that sequence before it names the override. Its decisions do not change.

The design adds no gate, refusal, stored state or approval. Limits stated and accepted: the bot's behaviour is taken from its documentation and was not checked in its code; a finding that returns under a new fingerprint is labelled again; a finding that returns although it was labelled is a bot defect, reported on slizard#3847; GitHub still shows a red check until the bot's next review. No leftover next-build.

## Summary

The SLizard review bot re-posts a P1 finding that was already answered on the pull request, on every push. Its check is not required, but it stays red, so GitHub shows the pull request as unstable. Split out of #6336 (pain P10) by operator decision on 2026-11-16.

## What we saw

- Wave 2a (2026-11-15/16), #6316 worker: an answered SLizard P1 came back on each push to the same pull request.
- The SLizard check stayed red on every head, and GitHub showed the pull request as unstable.
- Directive's own verdicts were not affected. `evaluateCiGate` excludes bot review checks from the CI verdict (`packages/core/src/pr-merge-readiness/ci-gate.ts`, `isBotReviewCheck`), and `pr:watch` reads the Greptile summary body.
- The design arc on #6336 found that printing the red bot check as advisory explains the state and does not remove the pain (audit comment 6907467218 on #6336).

## Expected

An answered finding does not come back as new on the next push, or the worker has one recorded way to mark it answered that the next review honours. The fix may belong in the bot, in its configuration, or in how the review cycle records an answered finding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a SLizard P1 finding that has a recorded answer on the pull request, when a new commit is pushed that does not change the lines the finding names, then the finding is not posted again as a new P1.
- Given a pull request whose only red check is the SLizard check for an answered finding, then the review-cycle documentation names the one step that clears it.
- Given the cause is in the bot and not in this repository, then this issue links the bot-side report and records the workaround.

Refs #6336. Refs #769.
